experiment: Diagnostic: Overlap-Resampled L-BFGS from Scratch (No Warmstart) on 2D Poisson

per_seed_results.note: Diverged after step 11003; 107 line search failures

analysis.from_scratch_converges: Partially. Seeds 0 and 1 converge to 9.5e-4 and 1.7e-3 respectively, but seed 2 diverges (best=3.8e-2, final=7.4e+19).
analysis.vs_warmstart: Warmstart overlap-LBFGS (7.03e-4) is ~19x better than from-scratch (1.36e-2) in mean rel L2. From-scratch has 11x more cautious skips (2752 vs 240) and much higher variance.
analysis.warmstart_role: Warmstart is critical for stability. Without it, L-BFGS from random init suffers from (1) high cautious skip rate (22-28% vs 2.9%), (2) occasional divergence (seed 2), and (3) much slower convergence. However, 2 of 3 seeds do reach reasonable solutions (within 2.4x of warmstart), suggesting the overlap mechanism does provide some benefit even from scratch.
analysis.conclusion: The Adam warmstart is critical rather than merely helpful. It provides: (a) a good initialization near a local basin, reducing cautious skips from 28% to 3%; (b) stability against divergence; (c) 19x better mean accuracy. The gains of the warmstart+overlap method come from both the warmstart AND the overlap mechanism, not the warmstart alone.
